claim: AMPL-MS is a novel antibody-based proximity biotinylation method that targets RNA and protein constituents of chromatin domains.
source: To gain molecular insight into these domains and explore their composition, we developed an antibody-based proximity biotinylation method targeting the RNA and proteins constituents. The method that we termed antibody-mediated proximity labelling coupled to mass spectrometry (AMPL-MS) does not require the expression of fusion proteins and therefore constitutes a versatile and very sensitive method to characterize the composition of chromatin domains based on specific signature proteins or histone modifications.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the development of AMPL-MS as a new method.

claim: AMPL-MS does not require the expression of fusion proteins.
source: The method that we termed antibody-mediated proximity labelling coupled to mass spectrometry (AMPL-MS) does not require the expression of fusion proteins and therefore constitutes a versatile and very sensitive method to characterize the composition of chromatin domains based on specific signature proteins or histone modifications.
evidence: The text explicitly states that AMPL-MS does not require fusion protein expression.

source: This analysis identified a number of known RNA-binding proteins in proximity of the hyperactive X and the centromere, supporting the accuracy of our method.
evidence: The abstract states that known RNA-binding proteins were identified, supporting the method's accuracy.

source: Characterization of these novel molecules suggested the formation of R-loops in centromeres, which we validated using a novel probe for R-loops in Drosophila.
evidence: The abstract states that characterization of the RNAs suggested R-loop formation, which was validated.

Consistent with the role of these histone modifications in establishing transcriptional active (H3K4me3 and H4K16ac) or repressive (H3K9me3) chromatin domains, the proteomic composition of these domains are very different (Figure 3a and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Nuclei were permeabilized with 0.25% Triton X-100 for 6 min on ice.
source: Following the treatment, the nuclei were permeabilized with 0.25% Triton X-100 for 6 min on ice and washed in assay buffer supplemented with 1% BSA (biotin-free BSA).
evidence: The methods section describes the permeabilization procedure.

claim: Antibodies were incubated with nuclei overnight in the cold room.
source: The respective antibodies were added (2.5 µg/reaction) and incubated overnight in the cold room on a rotating wheel.
evidence: The methods section describes the antibody incubation procedure.

claim: pA-Apex2 (2.5 µg) was incubated with nuclei for 2 hr in the cold room and another 1 hr in RT.
source: Next, the nuclei were incubated with 2.5 µg of pA-Apex2 in antibody incubation buffer for 2 hr in the cold room and another 1 hr in RT on a rotating wheel.
evidence: The methods section describes the pA-Apex2 incubation procedure.

claim: Biotinylation was performed by incubating nuclei with biotin-phenol (500 µM) for 20 min followed by H2O2 (1 mM) for 2 min.
source: The nuclei were first incubated with biotin-phenol (500 µM) in assay buffer for 20 min in RT in the dark, then H2O2 (1 mM) was added for 2 min to start the biotinylation reaction.
evidence: The methods section describes the biotinylation procedure.

claim: The biotinylation reaction was stopped by adding quenching buffer containing Trolox (5 mM), sodium ascorbate (10 mM), and sodium azide (10 mM).
source: The quenching buffer (Trolox 5 mM, sodium sscorbate 10 mM, sodium azide 10 mM) was added to stop the reaction.
evidence: The methods section describes the quenching procedure.

claim: Biotinylated proteins were isolated using streptavidin beads.
source: The rest of the lysate was incubated with 50 µl of precleaned streptavidin beads (Invitrogen, Dynabeads M-280 Streptavidin #11206D) at RT for 2 hr.
evidence: The methods section describes the protein isolation procedure.

claim: For RNA labeling, biotin-aniline was used instead of biotin-phenol.
source: The biotinylation reaction was performed using biotin-aniline (Iris Biotech, #LS-3970).
evidence: The methods section describes the RNA labeling procedure.

claim: Biotinylated RNA was enriched using C1 streptavidin magnetic beads.
source: To enrich biotinylated RNA C1 streptavidin magnetic beads (Invitrogen) were used (10 µl beads per 25 µg of RNA).
evidence: The methods section describes the RNA enrichment procedure.

claim: MaxQuant 1.6.1.476 was used to identify proteins and quantify by LFQ.
source: MaxQuant 1.6.1.476 (Tyanova et al., 2016) was used to identify proteins and quantify by LFQ with the following parameters: Database, dmel-all-translation-r6.08.fasta (Flybase); MS tolerance, 10 ppm; MS/MS tol, 20 ppm; Peptide false discovery rate (FDR), 0.1; Protein FDR, 0.01; Min. peptide length, 5; Variable modifications, Oxidation (M); Fixed modifications, Carbamidomethyl (C); Peptides for protein quantitation, razor and unique; Min. peptides, 1; Min. ratio count, 2.
evidence: The methods section describes the mass spectrometry data analysis procedure, with a citation.

claim: Proteins were considered significant if the LFC >1 and FDR ≤0.05.
source: Proteins were considered significant if the LFC >1 and FDR ≦0.05.
evidence: The methods section describes the statistical criteria for significance.

claim: Over representation analysis was performed using the enrichGO function from clusterProfiler package.
source: Over representation analysis was performed using the enrichGO function from clusterProfiler (Lyon et al., 2021) package v3.12.0 by taking the significant proteins (FDR 0.05 cut-off for predicted GO terms) and without a background set.
evidence: The methods section describes the GO analysis procedure, with a citation.

claim: The datasets produced in this study are available in the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the identifiers: PXD044295 (Proteomics) and PXD044296 (Histone PTMs).
source: The datasets produced in this study are available in the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE (Perez-Riverol et al., 2022) partner repository with the identifiers: PXD044295 (Proteomics) and PXD044296 (Histone PTMs).
evidence: The methods section describes data availability, with a citation.
